fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Matthew says, "His face shone like the sun…" Peter, James and John saw it right in front of them. I'd have needed oven mitts for my eyeballs.

Not this one, baker. The text says, "His face shone like the sun…" It describes a shine, and pale ash isn't in the picture. Ash is what I get when I forget the timer on a batch, and nothing about this scene looks like that.

You got it. "Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus." Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), and Elijah was a prophet (1 Kings 18:36). Two giants from Israel's long past, and they just show up on a mountaintop. I'd need a minute to sit down.

Altars sound very holy, friend, and I'd have guessed them too. But Peter never says that word. He says, "…I will put up three shelters…" Shelters are what he offers, and the text keeps it that simple.
Pillars aren't part of Peter's offer, baker. He says, "…I will put up three shelters…" Same plan, one for each of the three, but the word is shelters. Stone never gets mentioned.

Not this one, friend. The voice says, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!" Prophet isn't the word used. Elijah was a prophet (1 Kings 18:36) and he was right there on the mountain, but the voice speaks about Jesus as Son.

Good try, baker, but that's not the title. The voice from the cloud says, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." Servant is a fair guess, but the voice picks a different word, and it's a family word: Son. Then it adds that it is well pleased with Him.

Not quite, baker. Matthew says that when they looked up, "…they saw no one except Jesus." Moses and Elijah weren't among the ones they saw. When the three disciples looked up, the only one they saw was Jesus.

Good name, baker, but not the one Jesus means. Isaiah was a prophet (Matthew 3:3), but the text says the disciples understood "…He was speaking to them about John the Baptist." That's who Jesus was talking about.
